newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks close steady in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks close steady in heavy trade.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks eked out a slightly higher close on Tuesday, after swinging cautiouly in a narrow range in advance of a key U.S. inflation report due out later in the day, brokers said.

"If this CPI (consumer price index) report turns out to be non-event, I think we will see both the U.S. and Hong Kong markets move up again," said Charles Cheung, executive director at J&A Securities.
The Hang Seng Index scrapped out a 4.66-point advance to close at 13,293.87s but well off a low of 13,215.56. Turnover was a hefty HK$11.85 billion, slightly greater than Monday's HK$10.76 billion.

The U.S. consumer price index report for the month of December is due out later on Tuesday, and will be closely watched by U.S. financial markets and those overseas for clues on the future direction of inflation and interest rates, brokers said.

Turnover was augmented by a placement and new share issue of China Travel which eased HK$0.025 to close at HK$3.75 on trade of HK$1.91 billion. China Travel's parent placed out 420 million old shares at HK$3.60 each and subscribed for 700 million new shares at the same price.
Trade in Hang Seng Index futures, on the other hand, was modest with the January contract closing unchanged at 13,245 on trade of 10,888 and February finishing five points higher at 13,300.

The finance sector led the market, while utilities were sold off. HSBC Holdings closed HK$1.00 higher at HK$170.50, while Hongkong Telecom sank HK $0.30 to HK$13.05 on moderate turnover of HK$185.96 million.
Smaller banks were also very active. Guoco Group made the largest advance, closing HK$1.90 higher at HK$46.80 after setting an all time high of HK$47.20.
Dah Sing Financial jumped HK$1.50 to HK$32.80 a new high. Dao Heng Bank was boosted HK$1.30 to a new all time high of HK$40.30 then eased to close HK$1.10 higher at HK$40.10.
Brokers said a covered warrant on a basket of small and medium-sized banks was planned and then withdrawn.
Most brokers said they were marginally more optimistic on the outlook for property counters, which had been weighed down by concerns of possible government anti-speculation measures.
"The four major property developers have all fallen 10 percent from their all time highs," said J&A Cheung.

Brokers said property stocks should do well in advance of the new residential properties coming on the market at the end of January and in early February. Cheung Kong jumped HK$1.00 to HK$72.75 and Henderson Land rose HK$0.25 to HK$72.25. reuters
